column1: # Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam — Hadith 50: “Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah”

column2: From ʿAbdullāh ibn Busr, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Messenger of Allah, the laws of Islam have become too many for us; is there a comprehensive door we can hold fast to?
He said: “Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.” Imam Aḥmad recorded it with this wording.

Al-Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah and Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ recorded it with this meaning, and al-Tirmidhī said: Good and unusual (ḥasan gharīb). All of them recorded it through the narration of ʿAmr ibn Qays al-Kindī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Busr.

Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ and others recorded, from the hadith of Muʿādh ibn Jabal, that he said: The last thing on which I parted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was that I said to him: Which deeds are best and closest to Allah?
He said: “That you die while your tongue is moist with the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”
Many of the virtues of remembrance have already been mentioned here and there in this book; here we mention the virtue of keeping it up constantly and doing much of it.
Allah, Glorified is He, has commanded the believers to remember Him much, and has praised those who remember Him so.
The Exalted said: “O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance, and glorify Him morning and evening” [al-Aḥzāb 33:41–42]; and: “Remember Allah much, that you may prosper” [al-Anfāl 8:45];

and: “Men and women who remember Allah much — Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward” [al-Aḥzāb 33:35]; and: “Those who remember Allah standing, sitting and lying on their sides” [Āl ʿImrān 3:191].
In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from Abū Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a mountain called Jumdān and said: “Travel on — this is Jumdān. The mufarridūn [those who go apart] have gone ahead.”
They said: And who are the mufarridūn, Messenger of Allah?
He said: “The men and women who remember Allah much.”
Imam Aḥmad recorded it, and his wording is: “The mufarridūn have gone ahead.” They said: And what are the mufarridūn?
He said: “Those who are consumed (yuhtarūn) by the remembrance of Allah.”
Al-Tirmidhī recorded it, and in his version: They said: Messenger of Allah, and what are the mufarridūn? He said:
“Those who are infatuated (al-mustahtarūn) with the remembrance of Allah. Remembrance lifts their burdens from them, and they will come on the Day of Resurrection lightly laden.”

Mūsā ibn ʿUbaydah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Qarrāẓ, from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, who said: While we were travelling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ along the slope of Jumdān, he roused himself and said: “Muʿādh, where are those who went ahead?”
I said: They have gone on, and some people have fallen behind.
He said: “Muʿādh, those who go ahead are those who are infatuated with the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.” Jaʿfar al-Firyābī recorded it.

From this context the reason for mentioning “those who went ahead” in this hadith becomes clear. When the riders had gone ahead and some had fallen behind, the Prophet ﷺ pointed out that those who truly go ahead are the ones who constantly remember Allah and are devoted to it. For to be mustahtar about something

is to be devoted to it and enamoured of it, so that one hardly ever stops mentioning it. That is on the narration of those who transmitted it as “al-mustahtarūn”. Some transmitted it saying, “those who have been uhtirū in the remembrance of Allah,” and Ibn Qutaybah explained hatr as the rambling of dotage in speech, as in the hadith: “Two who revile each other are two devils, telling lies to each other and talking nonsense (yatahātarān).”

He said: What is meant by this hadith is those who lived long and grew old into dotage in the remembrance of Allah and obedience to Him. He said: On this narration, the mufarridūn are those left alone by their long life, apart from the generation they had lived among. As for the first narration,

the mufarridūn there are those who withdraw from people to remember Allah the Exalted. So he said. It is possible — and this is more likely — that on both narrations “going apart” means being singled out by this deed, namely abundant remembrance, rather than physical separation, whether from one's generation or from mixing with people. And Allah knows best.

In the same vein are the words of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz on the evening of ʿArafah, at ʿArafah, as the time of departure drew near: The one who goes ahead today is not the one whose camel goes ahead, but the one who is forgiven.
With the same chain, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever would like to graze in the meadows of Paradise, let him remember Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, much.”

Imam Aḥmad, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ recorded from the hadith of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do much of the lasting good deeds (al-bāqiyāt al-ṣāliḥāt).” He was asked: And what are they, Messenger of Allah?
He said: “Takbīr [Allāhu akbar], tasbīḥ [subḥān Allāh], tahlīl [lā ilāha illā Allāh], al-ḥamdu lillāh, and lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā billāh [there is no might and no power except through Allah].”
In the Musnad and Ṣaḥīḥ Ibn Ḥibbān, also from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Remember Allah so much that they say: He is mad.”
Abū Nuʿaym narrated in al-Ḥilyah, from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās as marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ): “Remember Allah so much that the hypocrites say: You are showing off.”
Imam Aḥmad and al-Tirmidhī recorded, from the hadith of Abū Saʿīd, that the Prophet ﷺ was asked: Which of the servants will be highest in rank with Allah on the Day of Resurrection?
He said: “Those who remember Allah much.” He was asked: Messenger of Allah, even above the one who fights in the path of Allah?
He said: “Even if he struck the disbelievers and idolaters with his sword until it broke and he was dyed with blood, those who remember Allah would be higher than him in rank.”
Imam Aḥmad recorded, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Muʿādh, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, that a man asked him: Which jihād has the greatest reward, Messenger of Allah?
He said: “That of those who remember Allah most.” He said: And which of those who fast have the greatest reward?
He said: “Those of them who remember Allah most.” Then he mentioned to us prayer, zakāh, Ḥajj and charity, and each time the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Those of them who remember Allah most.” Abū Bakr said: Abū Ḥafṣ, those who remember have carried off all the good! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Yes.”
Ibn al-Mubārak and Ibn Abī al-Dunyā recorded something with the same meaning by other routes, in mursal form.
In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to remember Allah at all times.
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: Those whose tongues remain moist with the remembrance of Allah — each of them will enter Paradise laughing. He was told: A man has freed a hundred slaves. He said:

A hundred slaves from one man's wealth is a great deal; but better than that is faith held to night and day, and that the tongue of each of you remain moist with the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
Muʿādh said: To remember Allah from early morning until night is dearer to me than to mount [fighters] on fine horses in the path of Allah from early morning until night.

Ibn Masʿūd said concerning the words of the Exalted, “Fear Allah as He truly deserves to be feared” [Āl ʿImrān 3:102]: That He be obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, thanked and not met with ingratitude. Al-Ḥākim recorded it as marfūʿ and declared it authentic, but it is better known as mawqūf (stopping short of the Prophet ﷺ).

Zayd ibn Aslam said: Mūsā (peace be upon him) said: My Lord, You have blessed me abundantly, so show me how to thank You abundantly. He said: Remember Me much. When you remember Me much, you have thanked Me; and when you forget Me, you have been ungrateful to Me.
Al-Ḥasan said: The dearest of Allah's servants to Allah are those who remember Him most and whose hearts are most God-fearing.

Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī said: Abū al-Mukhāriq told me: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I passed by a man hidden in the light of the Throne, and I said: Who is this? An angel?
I was told: No. I said: A prophet?
I was told: No. I said: Who is he?
He said: This is a man whose tongue was moist with the remembrance of Allah, whose heart was attached to the mosques, and who never caused his parents to be reviled.”
Ibn Masʿūd said: Mūsā (peace be upon him) said: My Lord, which deed is dearest to You for me to do?
He said: That you remember Me and do not forget Me.
Abū Isḥāq said, from Maytham: It has reached me that Mūsā (peace be upon him) said: My Lord, which of Your servants is dearest to You?
He said: The one who remembers Me most.
Kaʿb said: Whoever remembers Allah much is free of hypocrisy. Muʾammal narrated it from Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, as marfūʿ.
Al-Ṭabarānī recorded with this chain, as marfūʿ: “Whoever does not remember Allah much is free of faith.”
What supports this meaning is that Allah the Exalted described the hypocrites as remembering Allah only a little; so whoever remembers Allah much has parted from them in their qualities.

That is why Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn ends with the command to remember Allah: neither wealth nor children should divert the believer from it, and whoever is diverted by them from the remembrance of Allah is among the losers.
Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said, from one of his companions: The sign of love for Allah is much remembrance of Him, for you will never love anything without mentioning it often.

Fatḥ al-Mawṣilī said: The one who loves Allah is not heedless of the remembrance of Allah for the blink of an eye. Dhū al-Nūn said: Whoever has his heart and tongue occupied with remembrance, Allah casts into his heart the light of yearning for Him.

Ibrāhīm ibn al-Junayd said: It used to be said: Among the signs of one who loves Allah is constant remembrance with heart and tongue; and seldom is a person devoted to the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, without gaining from it the love of Allah.
One of the Salaf used to say in his intimate prayers: When the idle tire of their idleness, those who love You will never tire of conversing with You and remembering You.
Abū Jaʿfar al-Muḥawwalī said: The friend of Allah who loves Allah never has a heart empty of the remembrance of his Lord, and never tires of serving Him.

We have mentioned ʿĀʾishah's words: The Prophet ﷺ used to remember Allah at all times. That is, when standing, walking, sitting and lying down, and whether he was in a state of purity or of ritual impurity.
Misʿar said: The creatures of the sea would be still in the sea, while Yūsuf (peace be upon him), in prison, was never still from the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
Abū Hurayrah had a cord with two thousand knots in it, and he would not sleep until he had glorified Allah with it.

Khālid ibn Maʿdān used to say forty thousand tasbīḥs every day, besides what he recited of the Qurʾān. When he died and was laid on his bier to be washed, his finger kept moving as though counting tasbīḥ.
ʿUmayr ibn Hāniʾ was told: We never see your tongue slacken; how many tasbīḥs do you say each day?
He said: A hundred thousand, unless my fingers miscount — meaning that he counted them on his fingers.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Rawwād said: There was a woman with us in Makkah who used to say twelve thousand tasbīḥs every day. She died, and when she reached the grave she was snatched away from between the men's hands.

Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī would often say, when he was not narrating and had nothing to occupy him: Subḥān Allāh al-ʿAẓīm [Glory be to Allah the Magnificent]. This was mentioned to one of the jurists of Makkah, who said: Your companion is truly a man of understanding. No one says it seven times without a house being built for him in Paradise.
Most of what Ibn Sīrīn said was: Subḥān Allāh al-ʿAẓīm; subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdihi.
When all eyes were at rest, al-Mughīrah ibn Ḥakīm al-Ṣanʿānī would go down to the sea and stand in the water, remembering Allah along with the creatures of the sea.

Someone spent the night with Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, and said: Every time I woke in the night, I found him remembering Allah, and I would feel grieved; then I would console myself with this verse: “That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills.”

As for the lover, the name of his beloved is never absent from his heart. Were he required to forget it, he could not; and were he required to stop mentioning it with his tongue, he could not bear to.
How can the lover forget to mention a beloved / whose name is written in his heart?

Whenever the idolaters tortured Bilāl on the scorching sand for his belief in Allah's oneness, he would say: One, One! And when they told him to say “al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā”, he said: I do not know how to say that.
They would have the heart forget you, / but nature resists whoever tries to change it.
The stronger one's knowledge [of Allah], the more remembrance flows from the tongue of the one who remembers without effort, until one of them would say even in his sleep: Allah, Allah.

That is why the people of Paradise are inspired with tasbīḥ as they are inspired with breath, and lā ilāha illā Allāh becomes for them what cold water is for the people of this world. Al-Thawrī used to recite:
It is not that I forget You that I mention You so much; / it is simply that my tongue runs on it.

When the lover hears his beloved's name mentioned by someone else, his rapture grows and his longing doubles. The Prophet ﷺ said to Ibn Masʿūd: “Recite the Qurʾān to me.” He said: Shall I recite to you, when it was sent down to you? He said:
“I love to hear it from someone else.” So he recited to him, and his eyes overflowed with tears.
Al-Shiblī heard someone say, “O Allah, O Most Generous!” and he was shaken:
A caller cried out while we were at al-Khayf in Minā, / and stirred the heart's sorrows without knowing it.
He called someone else by the name of Laylā, and it was as if / for Laylā he set flying a bird that was in my breast.
The pulse races at the mention of the beloved:
When the beloved is mentioned in his lover's presence, / the drunken one sways and the enraptured one yearns.
The remembrance of lovers is unlike the remembrance of the heedless: “The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned” [al-Anfāl 8:2].
A tremor comes over me at the thought of you, / as a sparrow shakes itself when the rain has wet it.
One of the seven whom Allah will shade in His shade on the day when there is no shade but His is “a man who remembered Allah in solitude and his eyes overflowed.”

Abū al-Jald said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Mūsā (peace be upon him): When you remember Me, remember Me while your limbs tremble; be humble and tranquil when you remember Me; and when you remember Me, put your tongue behind your heart.
ʿAlī once described the Companions and said: When they remembered Allah, they swayed as trees sway on a day of strong wind, and their tears ran down onto their clothes.

Zuhayr al-Bābī said: Allah has servants who remembered Him and their souls departed out of reverence and yearning; and people who remembered Him and their hearts trembled with fear and awe, so that if they were burned with fire

they would not feel the touch of the fire; and others who remembered Him in winter and its cold and streamed with sweat out of fear of Him; and people who remembered Him and their colour turned dusty; and people who remembered Him and their eyes dried up from sleeplessness.
Abū Yazīd prayed Ẓuhr, and when he wanted to say the takbīr he could not, out of reverence for the name of Allah. He shook so violently that the rattling of his bones could be heard.
When Abū Ḥafṣ al-Naysābūrī remembered Allah, his state would change until everyone with him could see it. He used to say:

I do not think that anyone who truly remembers Allah, without heedlessness, could then remain alive — except the prophets, for they are supported by the strength of prophethood, and the elect among the friends of Allah, by the strength of their friendship with Him.
When she hears the Beloved's name, her joints / rattle at the awe of what she calls to mind.
Abū Yazīd stood one night until morning, striving to say lā ilāha illā Allāh, and could not, out of reverence and awe. When morning came, he went down and passed blood in his urine.
I never remember you but I forget you — / a forgetting of reverence, not a forgetting of neglect.
When I recall who you are and what I am, / I hold one like you too exalted to cross my mind.
Remembrance is the delight of the hearts of those who know Allah (al-ʿārifūn).
The Mighty and Majestic said: “Those who believe and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah — truly, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest” [al-Raʿd 13:28].
Mālik ibn Dīnār said: Those who take delight have taken delight in nothing like the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
In one of the earlier scriptures, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: O company of the truthful, rejoice in Me, and take your delight in remembering Me.
In another report, mentioned earlier: They turn to remembrance as eagles turn to their nests.

Ibn ʿUmar said: The People of the Book told me that this nation loves remembrance as the dove loves its nest, and that they are quicker to the remembrance of Allah than camels to their watering place on the day of their thirst.

The hearts of lovers find rest only in remembering Him, and the souls of those who yearn find peace only in seeing Him. Dhū al-Nūn said: This world is sweet only through remembering Him, the Hereafter only through His pardon, and Paradise only through seeing Him.
Ever do the souls of the seekers / long for the traces of your dwelling;
and so too do hearts, at the mention of you, / find rest after their fear.
They have gone mad with love of you — and who / loves the beloved and is not driven mad?
By your lives, my masters, / be generous with your nearness, and grant it as a favour.
The hadith “Remember Allah until they say: He is mad” has already been given. One poet said:
I have mentioned You so often / that people said: He is obsessed.
Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī used to remember Allah much. Someone saw him and found his state strange, and said to his companions: Is your companion mad?
Abū Muslim heard him and said: No, my brother; this is the cure for madness.
By the sanctity of love, I have no substitute for you, / and no aim, my masters, in anyone but you.
I made it a condition with the people whose company I kept / that my heart was yours and not theirs, and they agreed.
From the way I talk of you, they said: He has an illness. / I said: May that illness never leave me.
Lovers feel estranged from anything that distracts them from remembrance; nothing is dearer to them than being alone with their Beloved.
ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) said: O company of disciples, speak to Allah much and speak to people little. They said: How are we to speak to Allah much?
He said: Be alone to converse with Him; be alone to call on Him.

One of the Salaf used to pray a thousand rakʿahs every day until his legs gave way, and then he would pray a thousand rakʿahs sitting. When he had prayed ʿAṣr, he would sit with his knees drawn up, facing the qiblah, and say: I marvel at creatures — how can they find intimacy with other than You? Nay, I marvel at creatures — how can their hearts be illuminated by the remembrance of other than You?
One of them used to fast perpetually, and when it was time to break his fast he would say: I feel my soul leaving me, because eating distracts me from remembrance.
Muḥammad ibn al-Naḍr was asked: Do you not feel lonely on your own?
He said: How could I feel lonely, when He says: I am the companion of whoever remembers Me?
I hid the beloved's name from people / and kept my passion turning in my heart.
Oh, how I long for an empty land, / where I might call out the name of the one I love!

When the lover's state and knowledge grow strong, nothing distracts him from remembrance with heart and tongue. He is among people in body, while his heart is attached to the highest station, as ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said in describing them:
They kept company with this world with bodies whose souls were attached to the highest station. On this meaning it has been said:
My body is with me, but my soul is with you; / my body is in exile and my soul at home.
Another said:
I have made You the One who speaks with me in my heart, / and left my body free to whoever would sit with me.
My body keeps company with the one who sits with me, / while the Beloved of my heart is my companion within.
This was the state of the messengers and the truthful. The Exalted said: “O you who believe, when you meet a company [of the enemy], stand firm and remember Allah much” [al-Anfāl 8:45].
In al-Tirmidhī, as marfūʿ: “Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: My servant, truly My servant, is the one who remembers Me while he is meeting his opponent in battle.”

The Exalted said: “When you have finished the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting and lying on your sides” [al-Nisāʾ 4:103] — meaning the prayer in a state of fear; that is why He said: “Then, when you are secure, establish the prayer.” And the Exalted said, speaking of the Friday prayer:

“When the prayer is finished, disperse through the land, seek of Allah's bounty and remember Allah much, that you may prosper” [al-Jumuʿah 62:10]. So He commanded that seeking His bounty be combined with much remembrance of Him.
That is why the virtue of remembrance in markets and places of heedlessness has been reported, as in the Musnad, al-Tirmidhī and the Sunan of Ibn Mājah, from ʿUmar as marfūʿ:
“Whoever enters a market where there is shouting and selling and says: There is no god but Allah alone, without partner;

His is the dominion and His is the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is Living and does not die; in His hand is good, and He has power over all things — Allah will write for him a million good deeds, erase from him a million bad deeds and raise him a million degrees.”

In another hadith: “The one who remembers Allah among the heedless is like one who fights on behalf of those who flee; and the one who remembers Allah among the heedless is like a green tree amid dry trees.”
Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn Masʿūd said: So long as a man's heart is remembering Allah, he is in prayer, even if he is in the market; and if he moves his lips with it, that is better.
Some of the Salaf would go to the market deliberately in order to remember Allah there among the heedless.
Two of them met in the market, and one said to the other: Come, let us remember Allah while people are heedless. They went off to a secluded spot and remembered Allah,
then parted. Later one of them died, and the other met him in a dream, and he said to him: Did you know that Allah forgave us on the evening we met in the market?
Section: on the set portions of remembrance for the day and night. It is well known that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has obligated the Muslims to remember Him five times every day and night,

by performing the five prayers at their appointed times. Along with these five obligations, He has prescribed for them a remembrance that is supererogatory (nāfilah) — nāfilah meaning “addition” — so that it comes in addition to the five prayers. It is of two kinds.
The first is of the same kind as the prayer. He prescribed for them sunnah prayers along with the five prayers, before them, after them, or both before and after,
as an addition to the obligatory prayer: if there is a deficiency in the obligatory prayer, these voluntary prayers make it good; and if not, they are an addition to the obligations.

The longest intervals between the prayer times without an obligatory prayer are those between ʿIshāʾ and Fajr, and between Fajr and Ẓuhr. So in each of these two intervals a voluntary prayer was prescribed,
lest the time of heedlessness of remembrance grow long. Between ʿIshāʾ and Fajr He prescribed the witr prayer and the night prayer, and between Fajr and Ẓuhr the ḍuḥā prayer.

Some of these prayers are more emphasised than others. The most emphasised is the witr, which is why the scholars have disagreed over whether it is obligatory; then the night prayer, which the Prophet ﷺ kept up constantly, at home and on journeys;

then the ḍuḥā prayer, about which people have disagreed, as they have over whether it is recommended to keep it up constantly; there are authentic hadiths encouraging it. Encouragement has also been reported for praying just after the sun passes its zenith.
As for remembrance with the tongue, it is prescribed at all times, and more emphatically at some.
One of the times when it is more emphasised is after the obligatory prayers: Allah is to be remembered after each of them a hundred times, divided among tasbīḥ, taḥmīd, takbīr and tahlīl.

Remembrance is also recommended after the two prayers that are followed by no voluntary prayer, namely Fajr and ʿAṣr. Remembrance is prescribed after the Fajr prayer until the sun rises, and after ʿAṣr until the sun sets. These two times — I mean

the time of Fajr and the time of ʿAṣr — are the best times of the day for remembrance. That is why Allah the Exalted has commanded remembrance of Him in them in several places in the Qurʾān, such as His words: “And glorify Him morning and evening” [al-Aḥzāb 33:42]; “And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening” [al-Insān 76:25];

“And glorify [Him] in the evening and the early morning” [Āl ʿImrān 3:41]; “So he signalled to them: Glorify [Him] morning and evening” [Maryam 19:11]; “So glory be to Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning” [al-Rūm 30:17]; “And ask forgiveness for your sin, and glorify your Lord with praise in the evening and the early morning” [Ghāfir 40:55]; and His words:

“And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear, and without loudness of speech, in the mornings and the evenings, and do not be among the heedless” [al-Aʿrāf 7:205]; “And glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting” [Ṭāhā 20:130]; and “And glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before the setting” [Qāf 50:39].
The best remembrance done in these two times is the Fajr prayer and the ʿAṣr prayer, which are the best of the prayers.

It has been said of each of them that it is the middle prayer. They are the two cool prayers (al-bardān): whoever guards them will enter Paradise. After these two, the next time for remembrance is the night.
That is why the glorification and prayer of the night are mentioned in the Qurʾān after these two times.

Remembrance in general includes prayer, reciting the Qurʾān, learning it and teaching it, and beneficial knowledge, just as it includes tasbīḥ, takbīr and tahlīl. Some of the scholars of our [Ḥanbalī] school preferred recitation to tasbīḥ and the like after Fajr and ʿAṣr.
Al-Awzāʿī was asked about that and said: Their practice was the remembrance of Allah; but if one recites, that is good.

The apparent sense of this is that remembrance at this time is better than recitation. Isḥāq likewise said that saying tasbīḥ a hundred times after the obligatory prayers is better than recitation at that time.
The words of remembrance and supplications transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ for morning and evening are very many.

It is also recommended to spend the time between the two evening prayers in prayer and remembrance. The hadith of Anas has already been given, that the words of the Exalted were revealed about this: “Their sides forsake their beds” [al-Sajdah 32:16].

It is recommended to delay the ʿIshāʾ prayer until a third of the night has passed, as the authentic hadiths indicate — this is the position of Imam Aḥmad and others — so that this prayer is done at its best time, which is the end of its time,
and so that whoever is waiting for this prayer in congregation occupies this first third of the night with prayer, or with remembrance and waiting for the prayer in the mosque.
Then he prays ʿIshāʾ and, after it, the regular sunnah prayers that follow it, or he prays witr after that, if he wants to pray witr before sleeping.

When after that he goes to his bed to sleep, it is recommended that he sleep only in a state of purity and remembrance, saying subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh and Allāhu akbar to the full count of a hundred,
as the Prophet ﷺ taught Fāṭimah and ʿAlī to do when they went to sleep; that he say whatever he can of the words of remembrance reported from the Prophet ﷺ at sleep,
which are of many kinds, from recitation of the Qurʾān to remembrance of Allah; and that he then sleep in that state.

When he wakes in the night and turns over in his bed, let him remember Allah each time he turns over. In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, from ʿUbādah, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever wakes in the night and says: There is no god but Allah alone, without partner;

His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things; glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, and there is no might and no power except through Allah;
and then says, ‘My Lord, forgive me’ — or he said: and then supplicates — will be answered; and if he resolves [to pray], performs wuḍūʾ and prays, his prayer will be accepted.”
In al-Tirmidhī, from Abū Umāmah, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever goes to his bed in a state of purity, remembering Allah until drowsiness overtakes him,
will not turn over at any hour of the night asking Allah for any good of this world and the Hereafter without His giving it to him.”
Abū Dāwūd recorded something with this meaning from the hadith of Muʿādh, and al-Nasāʾī recorded it from the hadith of ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah.

Imam Aḥmad has, from the hadith of ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah, in this hadith: “and the first thing he says on waking is, ‘Glory be to You, there is no god but You; forgive me’ — he will shed his sins as a snake sheds its skin.”
It is established that when he ﷺ woke from his sleep he would say: “Praise be to Allah, who gave me life after He had caused me to die, and to Him is the resurrection.”

Then, when he gets up for wuḍūʾ and the night prayer (tahajjud), he does all of it as it has been reported from the Prophet ﷺ, and he ends his night prayer by seeking forgiveness in the hours before dawn, as Allah praised those who seek forgiveness before dawn. When dawn breaks, he prays the two rakʿahs of Fajr, then prays Fajr,
and after the Fajr prayer he occupies himself with the transmitted remembrance until the sun rises, as mentioned earlier. Whoever's state is as we have described,

his tongue will remain moist with the remembrance of Allah: he keeps remembrance with him while awake until he falls asleep upon it, and then begins with it when he wakes. That is one of the signs of true love, as one of them said:
You are the last thing in every slumber, / and the first thing at the time I wake.
Your remembrance is in my heart, asleep and awake; / for it the sides of the discerning forsake soft beds.
The second hemistich is obscure as printed (تجافى من اللّين اللبيب جنوب); it is translated in the sense that seems intended, echoing al-Sajdah 32:16 (“their sides forsake their beds”).
As for what a person does through the hours of night and day for the interests of his religion and his worldly life, the mention of Allah's name is prescribed over most of it.

He is prescribed to mention the name of Allah and praise Him over his eating, drinking, dressing, lying with his wife, entering his home and leaving it, entering the lavatory and leaving it, and mounting his riding animal; and he says the name of Allah over what he slaughters, whether as a rite or otherwise.
He is prescribed to praise Allah the Exalted when he sneezes, when he sees people afflicted in their religion or their worldly life, when he meets his brothers and they ask one another how they are,

and when there comes some fresh blessing he loves, or some affliction he dislikes is averted. More complete than that is to praise Allah in good times and bad, in hardship and ease, and to praise Him in every state.

He is prescribed to call on Allah the Exalted when entering the market, on hearing cocks crow at night, on hearing thunder, when rain falls, when the wind blows hard, on seeing the new moon, and on seeing the first fruits of the season.

Remembering Allah and calling on Him are also prescribed when distress descends and worldly calamities occur, when setting out on a journey, when stopping at halting places on a journey, and when returning from a journey.
Seeking refuge with Allah is prescribed when angry, on seeing something disliked in one's sleep, and on hearing dogs barking and donkeys braying at night.
Asking Allah for guidance in choosing (istikhārah) is prescribed when one resolves on something in which the better course is not clear.

Repentance to Allah and seeking His forgiveness are obligatory for all sins, small and great, as the Exalted said: “And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins” [Āl ʿImrān 3:135]. Whoever keeps to all this, his tongue will remain moist with the remembrance of Allah in all his states.
Section

We mentioned at the beginning of the book that the Prophet ﷺ was sent with comprehensive words. He ﷺ liked comprehensive forms of remembrance and chose them over other remembrance, as in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from Ibn ʿAbbās,

from Juwayriyah bint al-Ḥārith: The Prophet ﷺ left her early in the morning, when he had prayed Ṣubḥ, while she was in her place of prayer; then he came back after the forenoon had come, and she was still sitting there. He said: “Are you still in the state in which I left you?”

She said: Yes. The Prophet ﷺ said: “After leaving you I said four phrases, three times, which, if they were weighed against all you have said since this morning, would outweigh it: Subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdihi, as many times as the number of His creation, as much as pleases Him, as much as the weight of His Throne, and as much as the ink of His words.”

Al-Nasāʾī recorded it, and his wording is: “Subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh and Allāhu akbar, as many times as the number of His creation, as much as pleases Him, as much as the weight of His Throne, and as much as the ink of His words.”

Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī and al-Nasāʾī recorded, from the hadith of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, that he went in with the Prophet ﷺ to a woman who had date stones — or he said, pebbles — in front of her, with which she was glorifying Allah. He said: “Shall I not tell you of what is easier for you than this, and better?
Subḥān Allāh as many times as what He has created in the heaven; subḥān Allāh as many times as what He has created on the earth; subḥān Allāh as many times as what is between them;
subḥān Allāh as many times as what He is creating; Allāhu akbar the same; al-ḥamdu lillāh the same; and lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā billāh the same.”

Al-Tirmidhī recorded, from the hadith of Ṣafiyyah, that she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me when I had four thousand date stones in front of me with which I was glorifying Allah. I said: I have glorified [Allah] with these. He said: “Shall I not teach you something more than what you have glorified with?”
I said: Teach me. He said: “Say: Subḥān Allāh as many times as the number of His creation.”
Al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ recorded, from the hadith of Abū Umāmah, that the Prophet ﷺ passed by him while he was moving his lips, and said: “What are you saying, Abū Umāmah?”
He said: I am remembering my Lord. He said: “Shall I not tell you of what is more, and better, than your remembering through the night with the day and the day with the night?

That you say: Subḥān Allāh as many times as what He has created; subḥān Allāh filling what He has created; subḥān Allāh as many times as what is in the earth and the heaven; subḥān Allāh filling what is in the earth and the heaven;

subḥān Allāh as many times as what His Book has counted; subḥān Allāh filling what His Book has counted; subḥān Allāh as many times as everything; subḥān Allāh filling everything; and that you say al-ḥamdu lillāh the same.”
Al-Bazzār recorded something similar from the hadith of Abū al-Dardāʾ.
Ibn Abī al-Dunyā recorded, with a chain of his, that the Prophet ﷺ said to Muʿādh: “Muʿādh, how often do you remember your Lord each day?
Do you remember Him ten thousand times each day?”

He said: I do all of that. He said: “Shall I not direct you to words that are easier for you than ten thousand and ten thousand? That you say: Lā ilāha illā Allāh as many times as what He has counted; lā ilāha illā Allāh as many times as His words; lā ilāha illā Allāh as many times as His creation;

lā ilāha illā Allāh as much as the weight of His Throne; lā ilāha illā Allāh filling His heavens; lā ilāha illā Allāh filling His earth; lā ilāha illā Allāh the like of that along with it; Allāhu akbar the like of that along with it; and al-ḥamdu lillāh the like of that along with it.”
With his chain: A woman who glorified Allah with knotted threads was mentioned to Ibn Masʿūd, and he said: Shall I not direct you to what is better for you than that?

Subḥān Allāh filling the land and the sea; subḥān Allāh filling the heavens and the earth; subḥān Allāh as many times as His creation, and as much as pleases Him. Then you will have filled the land and the sea, the heaven and the earth.
With his chain, from al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān al-Taymī, who said: My father would narrate five hadiths and then say: Wait a moment. Subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, Allāhu akbar

and lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā billāh, as many times as what He has created and what He is creating, the weight of what He has created and the weight of what He is creating, filling what He has created and filling what He is creating, filling His heavens and filling His earth, and the like of that and many times that;

as many times as His creation, the weight of His Throne, the extent of His mercy, the ink of His words, the full measure of His good pleasure, until He is pleased and when He is pleased; as many times as His creation has remembered Him in all that has passed, and as many times as they will remember Him in all that remains;

in every year, month, week, day, night and hour, with every breath and every sigh, from eternity to eternity, the eternity of this world and the Hereafter, and a span beyond that whose beginning is never cut off and whose end never runs out.
With his chain, from al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān, who said: I saw ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Khālid after his death [in a dream] and said: How have you fared?
He said: Well. I said: Is there anything you would hope will help a sinner?
He said: Let him seek to learn the tasbīḥs of Abū al-Muʿtamir — what an excellent thing they are!

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn told me: One of the people of al-Baṣrah told me that Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd saw in a dream a man who had fallen in the land of the Byzantines, and said: What is the best of the deeds you have seen there?
He said: I have seen that the tasbīḥs of Abū al-Muʿtamir have a high standing with Allah.

Likewise the Prophet ﷺ liked the comprehensive forms of supplication. In the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ liked comprehensive supplications, and left aside whatever fell short of them.
Al-Firyābī and others recorded, also from the hadith of ʿĀʾishah, that the Prophet ﷺ said to her: “ʿĀʾishah, hold to the comprehensive supplications:

O Allah, I ask You for all good, immediate and deferred, what I know of it and what I do not know; and I seek refuge with You from all evil, immediate and deferred, what I know of it and what I do not know.

O Allah, I ask You for the good of what Your servant and Prophet Muḥammad asked You for, and I seek refuge with You from the evil of what Your servant and Prophet sought refuge from. O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and whatever word or deed brings one near to it, and I seek refuge with You from the Fire

and whatever word or deed brings one near to it; and I ask You, for whatever You decree for me, that You make its outcome right guidance.” Imam Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah, Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ and al-Ḥākim recorded it, but their versions do not mention comprehensive supplications; al-Ḥākim's has, “Hold to the complete ones (al-kawāmil),” and then gives it.
Abū Bakr al-Athram recorded it, and in his version the Prophet ﷺ said to her: “What kept you from taking the comprehensive words and their openings?”
and he mentioned this supplication.
Al-Tirmidhī recorded, from the hadith of Abū Umāmah, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a long supplication of which we memorised nothing.
We said: Messenger of Allah, you made a long supplication of which we memorised nothing. He said: “Shall I not direct you to what gathers all of it?

Say: O Allah, we ask You for the good of what Your Prophet Muḥammad asked You for, and we seek refuge with You from the evil of what Your Prophet Muḥammad sought refuge from. You are the One whose help is sought, it is for You to bring things to their end, and there is no might and no power except through Allah.”

Al-Ṭabarānī and others recorded, from the hadith of Umm Salamah, that the Prophet ﷺ used to say in a long supplication of his: “O Allah, I ask You for the openings of good, its conclusions and its comprehensive forms, its beginning and its end, its outward and its inward.”
In the Musnad: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ heard a son of his supplicating and saying: O Allah, I ask You for Paradise, its bliss, its brocade and the like,

and I seek refuge with You from the Fire, its chains and its shackles. He said: You have asked Allah for much good, and sought refuge with Allah from much evil; and I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

“There will be people who transgress in supplication” — and he recited this verse: “Call on your Lord humbly and in secret; He does not love the transgressors” [al-Aʿrāf 7:55] — “and it is enough for you to say:
O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and whatever word or deed brings one near to it, and I seek refuge with You from the Fire and whatever word or deed brings one near to it.”
In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: We used to say in the prayer behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Peace be upon Allah; peace be upon Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl;
peace be upon so-and-so and so-and-so. One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: “Allah is Himself al-Salām (Peace). So when one of you sits in the prayer,
let him say: All greetings, prayers and good things are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah —

for when he says it, it reaches every righteous servant of Allah in the heaven and the earth — I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger. Then let him choose whatever request he wishes.”
In the Musnad, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taught the openings of good and its comprehensive forms —

or: the comprehensive forms of good, its openings and its conclusions. We did not know what to say in our prayer until he taught us. He said: “Say: All greetings are for Allah…” and he gave it to the end. And Allah knows best.
